concepts.def: Doctrine of one God in three Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit; affirmed at Council of Nicaea 325 AD.
Belief that Jesus is God made flesh; 'the Word became flesh' (John 1:14); central to Christmas and Christology.
Jesus' death by crucifixion under Pontius Pilate and rising on the third day; 1 Corinthians 15 calls it 'of first importance'.
Reconciliation between God and humanity through Christ's sacrifice; Romans 5:8 'God showed his love while we were still sinners'.
Disobedience to God's will; original sin (Augustine) inherited from Adam and Eve; redeemed through Christ.
Doctrine of last things: Second Coming, Final Judgement, heaven and hell; Apostles' Creed affirms resurrection of the body.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity / Islam / Judaism / Buddhism / Hinduism / Sikhism: Social & Historical Developments — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Christianity / Islam / Judaism / Buddhism / Hinduism / Sikhism: Social & Historical Developments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Christianity / Islam / Judaism / Buddhism / Hinduism / Sikhism: Social & Historical Developments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does karma mean in Hindu and Buddhist thought?
options: Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Karma is when bad things happen to bad people as punishment.
The principle that actions have moral consequences shaping future experience or rebirth — not fate, but ethical cause and effect built into reality.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
